_note: Written by scripts/crate-calendar.mjs (run by publish-crate.mjs) from the Sigil NMF Crate. Do not edit by hand.

albums.title: Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album
albums.why: An official 34-track game soundtrack with Tame Impala, SZA, Justice and PinkPantheress among the names, not a Lana and Dua leak; neither is confirmed.

albums.title: Zion XII
albums.why: A producer beat tape in the J Dilla lineage; it won't have a lead rapper.

albums.title: Live at Max's Kansas City
albums.why: Suicide's frontman live, from Sacred Bones' archive series.

albums.title: anatole muster live
albums.why: A live trio set rather than a studio debut; it suits the jazz-adjacent lane.

albums.title: South of Dodge
albums.why: Confessional DIY indie in the Samia and Chastity Belt neighborhood; sources I read don't confirm the piano angle.

albums.title: Untitled
albums.why: Cincinnati honky-tonk songwriter, a favorite of John Prine's label. Your country wildcard.
A buzzing sophomore album from a guitar-forward London band, so it fits the new-artists lane.

albums.title: Green Island Days
albums.why: Warm, rhythmic folk with a Brazilian turn, so the Hermanos Gutiérrez comparison only half fits; think nylon-string warmth plus percussion, nearer Khruangbin's global side.

albums.title: One More Story
albums.why: Blu's laid-back LA storytelling. Short and easy to try.

albums.title: Blue Mountain (10th Anniversary Deluxe Edition)
albums.why: His cowboy-song solo record, expanded.

albums.title: Laughing at Noise
albums.why: Montreal dream pop that's buzzing on indie blogs.

albums.title: 22, A Million (10th Anniversary Edition)
albums.why: An anniversary edition of a record your Night Beds and Bon Iver comparisons keep pointing to.

albums.title: OTIS
albums.why: Gritty boom-bap with Daringer and Conductor Williams beats, close to the Black Milk and Blockhead lane, with a Goo Goo Dolls cameo as the oddity.

albums.title: Bad Throw, Good Catch
albums.why: A Wiltshire-born songwriter (not Irish) debuting on Island, recorded live to tape by a Big Thief producer, so squarely in your Dove Ellis and Villagers lane.

albums.title: Gilding the Lily
albums.why: London post-punk with big choruses.

albums.title: Rock of the Westies (50th Anniversary Edition)
albums.why: The 50th-anniversary expanded edition.

albums.title: The Easy Underground
albums.why: Brazilian-tinged vocal grooves, near Khruangbin and Jordan Rakei more than classic Thievery trip-hop.

albums.title: BAD BLADE
albums.why: A producer-led underground rap record with Quelle Chris and Boldy James features, squarely in your alt hip-hop lane (Aesop Rock, Black Milk, Blockhead).

albums.title: Blood On My Hands
albums.why: Not Jacob Lusk's voice this time. The band is now a duo with guest singers, including Brooklyn disco-soul group Say She She, which still sits near Thee Sacred Souls.

albums.title: Daughter From Hell (Deluxe)
albums.why: Dessner-produced confessional pop; a deluxe, so full list only.

albums.title: Surroundings
albums.why: Slow, immersive ambient in the Kelly Moran and Quiet Light lane, but built on field recordings and synth swells, with no piano to speak of.

albums.title: Switchblade Ballet
albums.why: DMV boom-bap. The hip-hop deep cut.

albums.title: Oxygène (50th Anniversary Edition)
albums.why: The synth classic turns 50.

albums.title: Joe Strummer 003: The 101'ers Years (1974-1976)
albums.why: Pre-Clash pub rock from the archive.

albums.title: If Ever You Would Leave Us (We Play for Rollins)
albums.why: A Sonny Rollins tribute on Blue Note. The jazz pick of the week for your Kamasi readers.

albums.title: Threshold (Original Motion Picture Score)
albums.why: Ambient score work from two artists in your electronic and ambient lane, near Kelly Moran and Quiet Light. Expect instrumental, film-driven pieces.

albums.title: Steps (Soundtrack from the Netflix Film)
albums.why: Bowers is an Oscar-winning composer, but this is a film score with a few pop songs; list it rather than expect a record.

albums.title: As Killers Do
albums.why: Lo-fi eight-track home recording with an Omnichord and fuzzy guitar. Leans more garage and dream pop than pure indie folk, so closer to Gia Margaret's homemade side than Big Thief's band sound.

albums.title: Demoed
albums.why: Kurt Wagner's songs sung by others, including MJ Lenderman and Alan Sparhawk (who also worked with Trampled by Turtles). Good for the americana and indie-folk side of your taste.

albums.title: Adieu False Heart
albums.why: Cajun-folk duets back on vinyl.

albums.title: All Ages
albums.why: Cerebral electronic left-field, closer to the adventurous end of your Sofia Kourtesis and Quiet Light lane than to club music.

albums.title: Find The Time
albums.why: A Canadian roots-pop songwriter.

albums.title: Electric Future Gangster
albums.why: Genre-blurring rap with soul and R&B leanings, in the lane of Vince Staples and Isaiah Rashad.

albums.title: Sweet Forever
albums.why: Warm, home-recorded vintage rock with Americana leanings and a Jim James cameo, a notch rootsier than the arena-size indie line suggests.

albums.title: Astra
albums.why: Left-field art-pop from a new voice, a good fit for the buzzing-new-artist lane, in the neighbourhood of Gia Margaret's quiet experiments.

albums.title: la forteresse
albums.why: Hushed French folk-pop in the Lucy Rose and Gia Margaret lane, now with a fantasy concept and her own hand on the production.

albums.title: Reveal (25th Anniversary Edition)
albums.why: Their underrated summer record gets the expanded treatment.

albums.title: E-Mortal Boy
albums.why: Afrobeats' biggest young star. For the readers who loved Tems and Tyla.

albums.title: Noon
albums.why: Dark, weather-heavy drone for the ambient lane. Far heavier than Kelly Moran or Quiet Light, so go in expecting slow and bleak.

albums.title: Harmacy (30th Anniversary Expanded Edition)
albums.why: Lo-fi indie rock history, expanded.

albums.title: Khudgarzi
albums.why: A brand-new voice in Arooj Aftab's orbit, since Aftab produced her earlier EP, with Raveena-style genre blending.

albums.title: Downside Up
albums.why: B-sides box set. Already a 90 critic score on AOTY.

albums.title: East Side Love Story
albums.why: An East LA Chicano-soul debut with Motown and G-funk in it, close to Thee Sacred Souls and Raveena.

albums.title: Dreamers
albums.why: Big UK pop release. Probably a skip for Sigil, listed for completeness.

albums.title: Love Century
albums.why: Murmur-era jangle from a band with Naima Bock in it; sits next to Local Natives, Land of Talk and Chastity Belt.

albums.title: Exploding In Slow Motion: The Complete Channel The Spirits Recordings
albums.why: Shabaka Hutchings' cosmic jazz trio, collected.

albums.title: Lucro Sucio; Unfinished Business
albums.why: A live document of the 2025 tour rather than a new record, so it fits the reissues and archives list, not the write-ups.

albums.title: Unusua
albums.why: Not the psych-pop Crumb and Khruangbin fans expect. This is a quiet, piano-led instrumental record, closer to your ambient lane (Kelly Moran, Quiet Light).

albums.title: Good Dogs
albums.why: Minnesota bluegrass-folk: your 'tour van full of banjos' lane.

albums.title: Jalsa
albums.why: Radiohead's guitarist with the Israeli songwriter, their second record together.

albums.title: Entropy
albums.why: The Australian psych band that changes style every record. Worth a look for the Geese crowd.

albums.title: Sentinel
albums.why: Experimental R&B with a gospel-trained voice. Short and easy to try.

albums.title: Decembers
albums.why: The Derry songwriter's warm, wry indie folk.

albums.title: Artifact
albums.why: The LA quartet's moody, groove-heavy indie rock. La Luz and Crumb fans take note.

albums.title: Somewhere Further Than Far Away
albums.why: The Seattle slowcore band whose members went on to Band of Horses. A Northwest pick.

albums.title: A Long Way from Kansas
albums.why: London synth-pop veterans. Near your Sylvan Esso picks.

albums.title: Happy Tears
albums.why: Scottish instrumental post-rock. A deep-listening option.

albums.title: Good Bye Make Party
albums.why: Minneapolis lyrical rap on Rhymesayers, Aesop Rock's label.

albums.title: Middle of Nowhere Vol. 2: Tex Mex Tapes
albums.why: The biggest country release on the calendar so far.

albums.title: Howl
albums.why: Jazz guitar, bossa nova and indie pop, sung in English and Japanese. A buzzing newer artist for the discovery slot.

albums.title: Star Echo Heavy Dove
albums.why: Chicago dream pop on Fire Talk.

albums.title: Ghost Coat
albums.why: Kate Stables' banjo-led folk band. Close to Bonny Light Horseman and Lucy Rose.

albums.title: Making American Music: The Smithsonian Sessions
albums.why: A Carolina Chocolate Drops co-founder on banjo. Your roots lane.

albums.title: AFTERBURNER
albums.why: Flatbush Zombies' producer-rapper. Your producer-album lane.

albums.title: Berlin, Berlin
albums.why: Irish folk songwriter Bon Iver has sampled.

albums.title: Eternity Shrugs
albums.why: Quiet Montreal folk-pop. The Gia Margaret and Lucy Rose end of your taste.

albums.title: SLUG
albums.why: The Belfast electronic duo. Your ODESZA and Sofia Kourtesis lane.

albums.title: Frog in the Belly of a Snake
albums.why: Intricate, fingerpicked folk.

albums.title: Spin
albums.why: A Toronto songwriter who works with BADBADNOTGOOD. Jazz-leaning and soft-spoken.

albums.title: Love Songs from the Hottest Summer on Record
albums.why: Noah Weinman's home-recorded indie folk, banjo included.

albums.title: Rollin' On
albums.why: An americana trio built on upright bass and harmonies. Tour-van folk.

albums.title: Forever Green
albums.why: The Detroit band that backed Waxahatchee on Saint Cloud. Easygoing folk-rock in your core lane.

albums.title: You Sing Like You're Joking
albums.why: El Kempner's indie rock project. Sharp songwriting in the Samia and Chastity Belt neighborhood.

albums.title: There Is a Light on the Horizon Line
albums.why: Adrianne Lenker co-produced her debut. Hushed, slow-burning folk.

albums.title: This World or the Next
albums.why: boygenius's Julien Baker, solo again. Sits right beside Big Thief and Waxahatchee in your core lane.

albums.title: Hover
albums.why: Woozy, jazzy indie pop. Close to Crumb.

albums.title: Bananas 4 Cats
albums.why: Indie pop with a big following. A reader-friendly pick.

albums.title: Blue Reservoir
albums.why: Tracey Thorn and Ben Watt's understated electronic pop.

albums.title: A Safe Place To Be Wild
albums.why: He's named in your taste profile's soul lane.

albums.title: What About Flamingos?
albums.why: Soul-pop with a jazz-school rhythm section.

albums.title: False Dogs
albums.why: English songwriter between folk and darker indie rock.

albums.title: Feat'Fòònese
albums.why: A Brazilian jazz pianist. For your Kamasi and Arooj Aftab readers.

albums.title: Darkening the Glass
albums.why: Chicago guitarist between folk, jazz and prog.

albums.title: Willing Brother Knowing
albums.why: He reworks old folk songs with banjo and fiddle. Andrew Bird fans should look.

albums.title: He's Gone
albums.why: Funk, Afrobeat and psych-soul. Khruangbin-adjacent.

albums.title: Impressiøn of a Human // Children of the Cørnerman
albums.why: Country songwriting with a grunge streak. The country wildcard.

albums.title: The Killing of a Motel Maid
albums.why: Willy Vlautin's Portland country-soul band. A Northwest pick.

albums.title: Silence, Please
albums.why: Canadian bluegrass with banjo and cello. Your tour-van folk lane.

albums.title: Compañero
albums.why: Big-hearted Australian indie rock. Local Natives energy.
